question: Which FTIR band did the authors use to tell whether PVDF remained in the reclaimed cathode powder, and for which filtration condition was that band absent?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE lower(text) LIKE '%ftir%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%cm%-1%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%cm−1%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%absent%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%disappear%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%band%' ORDER BY page, id
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=4 AND line_no BETWEEN 38 AND 60 OR (page=4 AND id IN ('p4.L42','p4.L43')) ORDER BY page, line_no

runs.text: The authors tracked PVDF with its characteristic FTIR band at

, which they assigned to PVDF (bending vibration of CH2). That band was present in the cathode rejects and in the powder filtered at room temperature, indicating PVDF was still there. It was absent for the reclaimed powder filtered at high temperature (hot filtration), which the authors took as evidence that the PVDF binder had been removed. In their words:

runs.quote: The absence of the typical band

runs.text: is the basis for this conclusion.

rendered: The authors tracked PVDF with its characteristic FTIR band at 871 cm^−1[1], which they assigned to PVDF (bending vibration of CH2). That band was present in the cathode rejects and in the powder filtered at room temperature, indicating PVDF was still there. It was absent for the reclaimed powder filtered at high temperature (hot filtration), which the authors took as evidence that the PVDF binder had been removed. In their words: The absence of the typical band[2] is the basis for this conclusion.

source.text: 871 cm^−1, indicating the existence of PVDF. This also demonstrates

citations.quote: The absence of the typical band

source.text: cooling down to room temperature. The absence of the typical band

citations.rendered: The absence of the typical band

expect: 871 cm^-1 (CH2 bending); absent for the powder filtered hot (~100 °C), present after room-temperature filtration (p4.L46-55)
